newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures seen opening flat to higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat to higher Wednesday after rising Tuesday on surging Southwest cash market prices due to tight supply and strong air-conditioning demand in the region.

In over-the-counter activity, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $35.75-36.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Tuesday's $35.45 and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $23.10-23.35 a MWh against yesterday's close at $23.24.
Analysts said the complex's downside risk continued to increase as more nuclear generation in the West is expected to return to operation from planned and unplanned outages.
Still market players are reluctant to sell due to a sharp spike in Southwest cash prices and short-term transmission difficulties on the Pacific Intertie, traders said.
Technically, August PV is expected to have enough momentum to test its life-of-contract high at $36.25 after just falling short by 15 cents yesterday, analysts said.
August COB would test $24.00 as an upside objective and $22.00 as a downside objective, they noted.
The 1,073 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant, in Avila Beach, California, held at 75 percent power as of early Wednesday.
Power production at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was still around 15 percent of capacity this morning, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 2 in Nevada, which tripped off line Monday due to a tube leak, was scheduled to restart later today.
Restarts of the 1,070 MW unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating (SONG) Station, in San Clemente, Calif., are set for July 15 and July 17.
SONG 2 was shut shut June 29 to replace charge line check valves, while SONG 3 has been out of service since April 12 for refueling, maintenance and replacement work.
Meteorologists called for cool, wet weather to linger over the Pacific Northwest into the weekend, followed by warmer, drier conditions next week.

Forecasters are split in their outlook for the Southwest. Some expected arid, seasonal weather to stay in the region through next week, while others predicted very hot weather stretching from California to much of Midwest.
